import sys, json, re

# The switch. It calls no model and reaches nothing: the class is decided from
# the ARGUMENTS the chat model already filled in, and from a table that lives
# right here.
#
# Every recipe declares its required parameters. A recipe that is NAMED but
# incomplete is an ERROR, never a downgrade into the design lane: a typo in one
# argument would otherwise silently buy an inference and answer a different
# question than the one that was asked.
RECIPES = {
    "rewire_edge":  ["scope", "from", "to", "old_to"],
    "add_node":     ["scope", "name", "template", "target", "route"],
    "attach_drain": ["scope", "from", "to", "route"],
    # A LEVEL is a recipe too, because the transit edges a new child gets belong
    # to the PARENT and are the same set every time. The renderer and its table
    # live in `recipes`; the counts live in the README, once. What is NOT decided
    # here is the template: that stays a catalogue question, and the catalogue is
    # the librarian's.
    "grow_level":   ["scope", "level", "name", "template"],
}

# The container a level is instantiated into, and the parameter it needs beyond
# the four above. Held here as well as in `recipes` on purpose: a recipe that is
# NAMED but incomplete must be refused at the switch, before an inference is
# bought, and the switch cannot ask the renderer.
LEVEL_EXTRA = {
    "org": [], "member": [], "assistant": [],
    # a channel needs the agent its turns default to; a CEL guard cannot read a
    # node's params, so the default lives as a literal on the edge that applies it
    "channel": ["assistant"],
    "screen": [],
    # an app writes onto ONE screen, and the edge that carries the view names it
    "app": ["screen"],
}

# GH #517 -- the CTX keys a level needs, held here for the same reason
# `LEVEL_EXTRA` is: a recipe that is NAMED but incomplete is refused at the
# switch, before an inference is bought, and the switch cannot ask the renderer.
# It is a ctx key rather than a parameter because the claim has to stand in the
# rendered manifest, where a reviewer sees it before it is committed.
#
# The round a channel's turns are spoken in used to be DERIVED from the last
# segment of the scope, which is right only while the member's directory happens
# to be spelled like the person. Where it was not, every row of the member's
# memory fell at the audience gate and the bundle read exactly like an empty
# store. A round is provenance; provenance is asked for, never invented.
LEVEL_CTX = {"channel": ["member_person"]}

# The question, verbatim on the wire and identical to the renderer's -- a
# refusal a human cannot read is one they cannot answer.
PERSON_QUESTION = (
    "who is the PERSON this channel speaks with? A channel's ingress edge "
    "declares the round every turn on it is spoken in -- "
    "[\"agent:<assistant>\", \"member:<person>\"] in affinity vocabulary -- "
    "and that round decides which rows of the member's memory the turn is "
    "allowed to see. It is the person's identity, which is NOT necessarily the "
    "name of the directory the member stands in. Name it as "
    "ctx.member_person of the wish.")

# The birth state a level may be grown into (GH #472). It is the mutation
# door's own vocabulary -- `add_nodes[].birth`, `active` (the door's default)
# or `inactive` -- and it is validated HERE, at the switch, for the same reason
# the level name is: a typo in one argument must not buy an inference and
# answer a different question than the one that was asked.
BIRTH_STATES = ("active", "inactive")

# The sentence a wish uses for it. A connector that must exist in the topology
# before its upstream is real is asked for in words rather than in a key, and
# the two spellings a request actually uses are the two that are read.
ASLEEP = re.compile(r"\b(?:born\s+)?asleep\b|\bborn\s+sleeping\b", re.IGNORECASE)
AWAKE = re.compile(r"\b(?:born\s+)?awake\b", re.IGNORECASE)

# "grow an assistant named scribe from assistant@2.2.0 under /os/orgs/acme/
# members/alex" -- the fast lane, recognised rather than inferred. It fires only
# when EVERY parameter it needs is in the sentence; a half-read wish falls
# through to the design lane, which is where an incomplete sentence belongs.
# This is not the same as the downgrade the rule above forbids: nothing was
# NAMED here, so nothing is being quietly re-asked of a model.
GROW = re.compile(
    r"\bgrow\s+(?:an?\s+|one\s+)?"
    r"(?P<level>org|organisation|organization|member|assistant|channel|screen|app)\b"
    r".*?\bnamed\s+(?P<name>[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)"
    r".*?\bfrom\s+(?P<template>[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*(?:@[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)?)"
    r".*?\bunder\s+(?P<scope>/[A-Za-z0-9/._-]*)",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
LEVEL_ALIAS = {"organisation": "org", "organization": "org"}

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
msgs = doc["body"].get("messages") or []
raw = ""
for m in msgs:
    if m.get("type") == "tool_call" and m.get("text"):
        raw = m["text"]
if not raw:
    for m in msgs:
        if m.get("text"):
            raw = m["text"]

try:
    args = json.loads(raw)
    if not isinstance(args, dict):
        args = {}
except Exception:
    args = {}


def emit(header, payload):
    # `operation` is on EVERY emission, because the hive's out-edges condition
    # on it. An edge that fired on "whatever is left over" would carry the day
    # somebody adds a fourth outcome.
    header["operation"] = "classify"
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": header,
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                      "text": json.dumps(payload), "id": ""}]}))
    sys.exit(0)


request = str(args.get("request") or "").strip()
if not request:
    emit({"route": "error", "error_code": "request_missing"},
         {"reason": "the tool call carried no request text"})

recipe = args.get("recipe")
if recipe:
    if recipe not in RECIPES:
        emit({"route": "error", "error_code": "recipe_unknown", "recipe": str(recipe)},
             {"reason": "no recipe by that name", "known": sorted(RECIPES)})
    params = args.get("params") if isinstance(args.get("params"), dict) else {}
    required = list(RECIPES[recipe])
    if recipe == "grow_level":
        level = str(params.get("level") or "")
        if level and level not in LEVEL_EXTRA:
            emit({"route": "error", "error_code": "level_unknown", "recipe": recipe},
                 {"reason": "no level by that name", "level": level,
                  "known": sorted(LEVEL_EXTRA)})
        required += LEVEL_EXTRA.get(level, [])
    if recipe == "grow_level" and params.get("birth") \
            and params.get("birth") not in BIRTH_STATES:
        emit({"route": "error", "error_code": "birth_unknown", "recipe": recipe},
             {"reason": "no birth state by that name",
              "birth": str(params.get("birth")), "known": sorted(BIRTH_STATES)})
    missing = [k for k in required if not params.get(k)]
    if missing:
        emit({"route": "error", "error_code": "recipe_params_incomplete", "recipe": recipe},
             {"reason": "the named recipe is missing parameters", "missing": missing,
              "required": required})
    # GH #517 -- and the ctx keys, under a code of their own. "You left out an
    # argument" and "the wish never said who is in the room" call for opposite
    # repairs: one is a typo in a tool call, the other is a question for whoever
    # made the wish, and it goes back in the words they have to answer.
    if recipe == "grow_level":
        given = params.get("ctx") if isinstance(params.get("ctx"), dict) else {}
        absent = [k for k in LEVEL_CTX.get(str(params.get("level") or ""), [])
                  if not str(given.get(k) or "").strip()]
        if absent:
            emit({"route": "error", "error_code": "wish_incomplete", "recipe": recipe},
                 {"reason": PERSON_QUESTION,
                  "missing": ["ctx.%s" % k for k in absent]})
    emit({"route": "recipe", "recipe": recipe},
         {"recipe": recipe, "params": params, "request": request})

# Nobody NAMED a recipe. Before the design lane buys an inference, the sentence
# is read once for the one shape that is entirely deterministic: growing a child
# into a level. A match renders; anything else -- including a sentence that names
# a level and forgets the template -- goes on to the model, exactly as before.
if not recipe:
    hit = GROW.search(request)
    if hit:
        found = hit.groupdict()
        level = LEVEL_ALIAS.get(found["level"].lower(), found["level"].lower())
        grown = {"scope": found["scope"], "level": level,
                 "name": found["name"], "template": found["template"]}
        for key in ("ctx", "override_params", "assistant", "screen",
                    "birth", "subscribe", "credential"):
            value = args.get(key)
            if value:
                grown[key] = value
        if grown.get("birth") and grown["birth"] not in BIRTH_STATES:
            emit({"route": "error", "error_code": "birth_unknown",
                  "recipe": "grow_level"},
                 {"reason": "no birth state by that name",
                  "birth": str(grown["birth"]), "known": sorted(BIRTH_STATES)})
        # The key wins over the words: an argument the caller filled in is a
        # decision, a sentence is a reading of one.
        if not grown.get("birth"):
            if ASLEEP.search(request):
                grown["birth"] = "inactive"
            elif AWAKE.search(request):
                grown["birth"] = "active"
        # GH #517 -- a sentence that names no person is not complete for the
        # fast lane either, and here that is NOT an error: nobody named a
        # recipe, so nothing is being quietly re-asked. It falls through to the
        # design lane, whose composer asks the same question out of the brief.
        given = grown.get("ctx") if isinstance(grown.get("ctx"), dict) else {}
        told = all(str(given.get(k) or "").strip() for k in LEVEL_CTX.get(level, []))
        if told and all(grown.get(k) for k in RECIPES["grow_level"] + LEVEL_EXTRA[level]):
            emit({"route": "recipe", "recipe": "grow_level"},
                 {"recipe": "grow_level", "params": grown, "request": request})

# The design lane hands the request on as a plain USER turn. The librarian
# tokenises the first turn that carries text for its BM25 query, and `brief`
# looks for `origin == "user"` -- a json blob in that slot would be tokenised
# as `request`, `scope` and a pile of punctuation, which is the query the
# librarian exists to serve turned into noise. The scope travels in the
# CONTEXT compartment instead, where it survives the hops that hop does not.
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": {"route": "design", "operation": "classify",
               "build_scope": str(args.get("scope") or "/")},
    "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text", "id": "", "text": request}]}))

description.purpose: The switch of the builder: it reads the arguments of the build_topology tool call and decides the CLASS of the request -- a named recipe whose parameters are complete takes the fast lane, a sentence that is exactly "grow a <level> named <name> from <template> under <path>" is recognised as one, and everything else takes the design lane. It calls no model and reads nothing but the message.
description.use_when: First cell behind the builder's door, on `in_build`.
description.not_in_scope: No rendering, no retrieval, no inference, and no downgrade: a named recipe that is missing a parameter is refused by name rather than quietly re-asked of a model. The recognised grow sentence is not that downgrade in reverse -- it fires only when every parameter it needs is in the sentence, and a half-read wish falls through to the design lane, which is where an incomplete sentence belongs.
